M14.0.SPEC (#419) — toml completeness classification. Every public NAMED node type of the pinned wasm/tree-sitter-toml.wasm is in exactly one bucket. The grammar exposes 20 nodeTypeForId slots but only 19 DISTINCT names: `escape_sequence` is declared twice, which is a grammar quirk rather than two node types. MEASURED, not restated (2026-10-09, commit 840bffea9): enumerating wasm/tree-sitter-toml.wasm through web-tree-sitter's Language API gives 66 node-type slots, of which 20 are NAMED and 19 are distinct named names — exactly the claim above, with the anonymous punctuation tokens making up the remaining 46 slots (44 distinct). ERROR and MISSING are injected by this gate for EVERY language because the wasm ABI does not list them; neither occurs for this grammar and both are silent here. Silence is guilt: a type in no bucket fails section A, and a type the wasm no longer produces is a stale row and also fails. That rule bites hardest on the four DATETIME types — none appears anywhere in cargo's 684 files, so their handling is pinned by FIXTURE rather than by the corpus, and a corpus-only lane would have classified them by assumption and called it coverage. SECTION D WAS RED, AND THIS REVISION CLOSES IT WITH THE CONSTRUCT THAT EARNED THE SECOND TIER. The gate requires >=2 distinct `evidenceClass` values; when this rationale was written every edge the lane emitted was `structural`, and both dishonest routes were refused: a `uses` edge for a path-shaped string, and `inferred` on an implied parent. What closed it was NOT a single-tier allowance — TOML grew the construct. A Cargo `path` dependency (`core = { path = "../core" }`) names a FILE the document itself writes, which the fleet vocabulary (`script/m14/audit-analyzer-grammar.ts:146`) defines as `import_based`; the lane already emitted and pinned those edges as `imports` (`dependencyFileClaim` checks the target against the project's admitted files, `sourcePathClaim` covers the refuted remainder), and classing them `structural` was the MISCLASSIFICATION — `structural` is for facts that need nothing outside the file, and a path dependency's whole point is that it points outside it. The analyzer now writes `import_based` for that edge and four `imports` rows in `validation/m14/fixtures/toml/path-dependencies.expectation.json` pin it, so section D reads `2 tier(s) pinned: import_based, structural`. NOTHING ELSE MOVED: section B's emitted/pinned set is unchanged, the `exports` guard is untouched (still NOT-DOABLE to emit AND resolve, settled by the mutant in CALLS-REFERENCES-AND-TOML.md §2), fixtures read 10/10 before and after, and the edge count is unchanged. E and F are the canonical F5 ceremony, exactly as for html.

handled_verified.note: Twenty-one types, each read in src/ast/real-toml-analyzer.ts and each pinned. `ERROR` is handled for the corpus reason recorded on the internal_silent side, and the analyzer now walks for recovery nodes itself — REPORTED at the node's OWN span, BYPASSED, and everything AROUND it still published. It had been pushing no diagnostics at all, so the "reported" half of the contract was entirely the engine's: a contract resting on a caller is not a contract, which is the same blindness the svelte lane had in the opposite direction. `children`, not `namedChild`, because the expected token of a MISSING node can be anonymous. Pinned by `toml/malformed-and-rejected` and `toml/error-node-becomes-symbol`. DECLARED CONSEQUENCE OF THE BYPASS, measured rather than assumed: a key whose VALUE fails to parse is not published. The whole `key = invalid-value` pair sits inside the ERROR, and the walk does not descend into one, so `invalid-section.key` is absent from a document whose table and every earlier key are present. Measured over the whole pool this costs exactly TWO symbols in TWO files, both cargo's own invalid-manifest fixtures. It is declared rather than repaired because recovering the key means inferring table scope from POSITION inside a region the parser marked unreadable — the ERROR sits at document level, so ownership would have to come from "the last header before this offset", and a wrong guess attaches a real key to the wrong table. Two symbols in two intentionally-broken files does not justify that risk, and the alternative is not silence: the file is reported with a parse error at the key's own line. DECLARED, ZERO CORPUS OCCURRENCES: an unterminated header such as `[bad` is recovered by the grammar into a real `table` node whose header children include an ERROR, and a following genuine header is nested inside that ERROR. Read naively the analyzer would publish the invented table and lose the real one. Measured across all 743 files this shape occurs ZERO times, so no behaviour is changed on the strength of a synthetic input — the same discipline that removed the values-as-symbols mutant rather than fixing it, on the grounds that the measured enter state is stronger evidence than a stand-in. It is recorded so a future corpus that does contain the shape inherits the decision instead of rediscovering it.

internal_silent.note: MISSING and `comment` are two types that correctly emit nothing and need no analyzer read. `comment` is a literal: a comment is not an identity, and TOML has no block-comment form, so a `#` line contributes nothing to the graph. MISSING holds across the whole 743-file pool — zero MISSING nodes, and it is a property of this grammar that a recovery node is always a full ERROR rather than an inserted token. ERROR WAS HERE AND WAS WRONG, and the correction is recorded because the reasoning that put it here is the exact trap the svelte lane fell into on the same day. This note previously read "NEITHER OCCURS for this grammar", on the evidence of TWELVE HAND-MADE MALFORMED DOCUMENTS. The corpus was never measured. Measuring it: 2 of 743 files (0.27%) carry an ERROR node — `cargo/tests/testsuite/cargo_add/invalid_manifest/{in,out}/Cargo.toml`, cargo's own deliberately-invalid manifest fixtures, where `key = invalid-value` is a bare word where TOML requires a value. Two hand-made malformed documents and 743 real ones disagreed, and the real ones were right. ERROR now sits in handled_verified, and the analyzer reports it itself rather than leaving the whole contract to the engine.

decisions.question: Should the analyzer decode a quoted key's escapes by WALKING its `escape_sequence` child nodes, or by decoding the quoted_key's own text in pure-String?
decisions.ruling: RULED: decode the PARENT'S TEXT, in pure-String, and never walk `escape_sequence`. The two are equivalent by construction — an escape_sequence node's text is exactly the escape sequence its parent contains — so walking the children would buy nothing and cost a second pass over every quoted key. It would also put the lane's no-regex rule under pressure: the natural way to express a decode is a replacement pattern, and that rule exists because every regex literal is one more thing to audit for backtracking. The decode handles the escapes TOML defines in a key (\n, \t, \r, \", \\, \uXXXX) and passes an UNKNOWN escape through with its backslash rather than dropping it, because silently discarding half a key would invent a different identity. Measured: `"a\u0062c"` resolves to the single key `abc`, and a literal-string key takes a pure slice because a literal string has no escapes at all.
decisions.consequence: `escape_sequence` is classified HERE rather than as handled, so the type is accounted for exactly once and the reason it is not walked is on the record rather than being invisible.

zeroEmissionFacts.label: decorates
zeroEmissionFacts.from: validation/m14/measurements/toml-extended-constructs-census.json — extended.decorator: 0 `toml.decorator_shaped_key_whose_value_is_an_applied_call` sites over the whole admitted population (1,485 .toml files / 77 repos, production parseFile, 0 parse failures); the near miss is 1 decorator-shaped key site (gql-gqlgen/.mdformat.toml:26 `wrap="keep"`, a NAME/pointer, not an application); 580 call-shaped text values but 0 non-literal values in the whole corpus (the grammar's value production set is closed over literals and containers: array, inline_table, string, integer, float, boolean and the four datetime types — 19 named node types in the served build's own inventory, sha256 7849ac8ce9d10a46)
zeroEmissionFacts.statement: `decorates` is an APPLIED CALLABLE: the contract says the source is the decorated declaration and the target is the decorator's name, applied by the runtime while the declaration is created — the decorated symbol does not invoke it. TOML has no expression production of any kind: every value is a literal or a container of literals (the grammar's closed value set is the 8 types listed above), so there is no syntax in which a key's value could APPLY a callable. The csharp dialect the fleet accepted twice decides the nearest neighbour: IF THE VALUE IS A CALL IT IS AN APPLICATION; IF IT IS A PLAIN NAME IT IS A POINTER. The corpus has exactly one decorator-shaped key and its value is a plain name — a pointer, not an application — and the 580 call-shaped text values are all strings carrying text that merely looks like a call (coordinates, format strings, CSS-like values), each a lexed `string` node and never an applied anything. LADDER, WALKED: R1 unavailable — no tree-sitter-toml build spells an expression or call production (the served build's own inventory is 19 named types, none of them a call, an expression or an application); R2 unavailable — a patch would have to invent syntax the language does not have (TOML 1.0's grammar has no expression form, so the patch would define a new language, not TOML); R3 unavailable — no existing node type carries the relation (a `pair` whose value is a `string` is a data assignment, and reading a decorator application out of it would be the fabrication the csharp ruling refuses).
zeroEmissionFacts.falsifier: A decorator-shaped key (`decorator`, `decorate`, `annotation`, `wrap`, `middleware`, `prepend`, `hook` …) whose VALUE is an applied call — i.e. a value the grammar parses as something other than a literal or a container, the only shape an application can take in a language with no expressions. THE CONSTRUCT IS COUNTED: `toml.decorator_shaped_key_whose_value_is_an_applied_call` (a decorator-shaped key whose value node's type is outside the grammar's closed value set), with `nonLiteralValues` counting every non-literal value in the corpus beside it, so the zero is a measurement rather than a matcher that never fired. If either count is NON-ZERO the application shape is reachable and `decorates` must be implemented instead of ruled.
zeroEmissionFacts.grammarInventory: 19 named node types (of 66 slots, 20 named, 1 duplicate named slot) in the served build's own inventory, sha256 7849ac8ce9d10a46 — none is an expression, a call or an application

zeroEmissionFacts.label: renders
zeroEmissionFacts.from: validation/m14/measurements/toml-extended-constructs-census.json — extended.template: 0 template tokens that BOTH parse outside every string/comment AND sit in no ERROR region over the whole admitted population (1,485 .toml files / 77 repos); 508 template tokens total in 159 files, of which 410 are INSIDE a lexed `string` (text carried as data), 3 in comments, and of the 95 outside both, 92 are inside an ERROR region the parser marked unreadable (another language's text inside a TOML file) and the remaining 3 are brace-collision fragments the parser happened to fold into an `inline_table` (Go-template `{{end}}]` tails and `precedence = {{ .Precedence }}` in traefik integration fixtures) — template text the grammar could not lex, each inside a pair whose document carries an ERROR elsewhere
zeroEmissionFacts.statement: `renders` is the name in a RETURNED CONSTRUCTION: the source is the rendering symbol and the target is the rendered component, and the fleet's four implementations agree on the shape (a JSX tag, a hiccup vector, a type argument, dart's `build` returning a Widget) — a template expression that NAMES A COMPONENT. Template text IS present in the corpus's TOML files (`{{range .SANs }}`, `{{ .Precedence }}` in traefik fixtures, `${...}` in others) AND THE GRAMMAR CANNOT LEX IT: 92 of the 95 tokens that sit outside every string sit inside an ERROR region, and the 3 that do not are the closing braces of the same unlexable spans (the parser folded `{{end}}]` into a pair whose value node reads as an inline table — a recovery artefact of the SAME unreadable region, not a TOML value). A component-naming interpolation is therefore ANOTHER LANGUAGE'S TEXT INSIDE A TOML FILE, not a TOML construct, and a TOML document has no expression to return a construction from. LADDER, WALKED: R1 unavailable — no tree-sitter-toml build lexes a template interpolation (the served build's inventory has no such production and every template token outside a string lands in an ERROR); R2 unavailable — a patch would have to invent an expression/template syntax the language does not have (TOML 1.0 has no interpolation; the corpus's templates are Go-template text processed by tools OUTSIDE the document); R3 unavailable — no existing node type carries the relation (an `inline_table` or `string` value is data, and no node type names a component).
zeroEmissionFacts.falsifier: A template expression that NAMES A COMPONENT and is LEXED AS A TOML VALUE — a token outside every string AND outside every ERROR region, so the grammar parsed it rather than refusing it. THE CONSTRUCT IS COUNTED: `toml.template_token_lexed_outside_every_string_and_error_region`, measured against `toml.template_token_inside_a_lexed_string` (410) and `toml.template_token_inside_an_error_region` (92) so all three positions are measured and the difference between them IS the ruling. If the lexed-outside count is NON-ZERO then an interpolation IS a TOML value and `renders` must be implemented instead of ruled.
zeroEmissionFacts.grammarInventory: 19 named node types (of 66 slots) in the served build's own inventory, sha256 7849ac8ce9d10a46 — none is an expression, a template or an interpolation production

zeroEmissionFacts.label: mixes_in
zeroEmissionFacts.from: validation/m14/measurements/toml-extended-constructs-census.json — extended.mixinDecisive: 0 tables carrying BOTH a component list AND a separately named base over the whole admitted population (1,485 .toml files / 77 repos); the near miss is 2 tables carrying a component list ([tool.mypy] with `plugins = [...]` in gql-saleor/pyproject.toml, [toolchain] with `components = [...]` in hasura-engine/v3/rust-toolchain.toml), each naming tools' plugin lists and each with NO base clause in the same table
zeroEmissionFacts.statement: The vocabulary's own reason a mixin is not `extends` is that THERE IS NO SINGLE BASE and the component list is attached SEPARATE from the base clause — so the mixin shape is a LIST OF COMPONENTS ATTACHED BESIDE A BASE. A TOML table is a flat key/value namespace: it has no type, no base and no composition production, and the only component-list shape the corpus carries (2 tables) names TOOL PLUGIN lists — `plugins` for mypy, `components` for rustup — which are consumed by the tool at its own runtime, with no supertype chain and no base in the same table. YAML's merge key is a composition production of the format; TOML has none, so there is nothing for a mixin to compose into. LADDER, WALKED: R1 unavailable — no tree-sitter-toml build spells a composition or base-clause production (the served build's 19 named types are values, containers and keys); R2 unavailable — a patch would have to invent a composition semantics the language does not have (no TOML version defines table inheritance or composition); R3 unavailable — no existing node type carries the relation (a `pair` holding an `array` of strings is a list value, and a list of plugin names beside NOTHING is a flat namespace, not a mixin).

zeroEmissionFacts.statement: `part_of` is the shared-scope relation: a part SHARES the library's single scope, imports nothing, and cannot be resolved as a separate module, and the direction is the directive's own. TOML HAS NO INCLUDE DIRECTIVE: the grammar's own inventory (19 named node types, enumerated through the Language API over the served build) has no production that splices another document's text into this one, and RFC 8259-style TOML defines no inclusion — the format's unit is the whole document. The near-miss shape is measured and refused on the contract's own test: a key whose value NAMES a file (1,074 sites, 442 files) puts the fragment at a KEY POSITION as a VALUE consumed by a tool, never at the including document's top level, so no scope is shared — the same ground the yaml lane's `!include` ruling rests on, with the added fact that TOML's file-naming keys are plain strings with no tag semantics at all.
